paper_metadata.title: Hybrid Photonic Quantum Reservoir Computing for High-Dimensional Financial Surface Prediction

experiments.description: Main hybrid photonic quantum reservoir computing (QORC) experiment for next-day swaption surface prediction using an ensemble of three fixed photonic reservoirs, a sparse denoising autoencoder, and Ridge regression readout.

algorithm.variant: Ensemble photonic quantum reservoir computing with sandwich linear-optical circuits and Ridge readout
algorithm.ansatz: Fixed linear optical sandwich circuit U_rand · PS(phi) · U_rand
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Closed-form Ridge solution; no iterative quantum training
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Fixed Haar-random unitaries after initialization; orthogonal projection matrix W with orthonormal rows; no trainable quantum parameters

problem_formulation.encoding_details: The 120-dimensional classical context vector is projected to m modes by a fixed orthogonal map and mapped to phases via phi_i = 2π · sigmoid(sum_j W_ij x_j). The photonic circuit then measures Fock-basis output probabilities.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Predict next-day latent code z_{t+1} from past latent codes and quantum features, then reconstruct the next-day swaption surface via the decoder.

problem_instance.description: Next-day prediction of 224-dimensional swaption surfaces from historical daily surfaces.

dataset_specification.description: 494 daily trading surfaces, each a 14×16 grid vectorized to 224 prices; 6 future trading days held out for test; training uses 439 windows and validation uses last 50 windows after temporal windowing.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Three-stage preprocessing: winsorization at 1st/99th percentiles fitted on training data, robust scaling by median and IQR, then min-max normalization to [0,1]. Sparse denoising autoencoder trained with 15% random masking of inputs.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Single held-out test set of 6 future days with walk-forward evaluation; metrics reported as latent MSE, surface RMSE, R2, training time, and inference latency.

noise_model.noise_description: classically simulated photonic circuits; no explicit noise model reported

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Winsorization, robust scaling, min-max normalization, sparse denoising autoencoder, temporal windowing with k=5 and first-difference momentum term, feature standardization for quantum outputs
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Decoder reconstructs 224-dimensional surface from predicted latent code; inverse transform back to original price scale

speedup_claims.conditions: inference latency comparison on the held-out test setting
speedup_claims.caveats: Based on reported per-sample inference latencies; quantum feature extraction is classically simulated in this paper.

speedup_claims.caveats: Reported latency excludes any real photonic hardware overhead.

speedup_claims.conditions: inference latency comparison on the held-out test setting
speedup_claims.caveats: Random Forest inference is particularly slow in this benchmark; comparison is per-sample latency.

speedup_claims.conditions: inference latency comparison on the held-out test setting
speedup_claims.caveats: QORC + Ridge is still sub-millisecond, but not the fastest model.

speedup_claims.conditions: for Fock-basis probability computation in photonic circuits
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a complexity-theoretic claim, not an empirical speedup measurement.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Classical simulation of Fock probabilities scales as O((n+m-1 choose n))
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: Approximately 26,700 floating-point operations for the Ridge readout per sample
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_quantum: 0.10 ms inference latency reported for the full hybrid model
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_classical: 0.06 ms inference latency for classical Ridge baseline

experiments.description: Simplified photonic reservoir ablation using a single fixed linear-optical reservoir without the sandwich architecture, followed by Ridge regression.

algorithm.ansatz: Single random unitary U_rand in U(12) with phase encoding
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Closed-form Ridge solution; no iterative quantum training
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Single Haar-random unitary after initialization; fixed thereafter

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same 120-dimensional classical context is projected to 12 modes and encoded as phases; Fock-basis probabilities are used as features.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Predict next-day latent code z_{t+1} from photonic features and reconstruct the swaption surface.

experiments.description: Variational photonic quantum circuit baseline trained end-to-end to predict swaption latent codes from classical context.

algorithm.ansatz: Photonic variational circuit with beam splitter angles and phase shifter settings; 4 variational layers

problem_formulation.encoding_details: The 120-dimensional classical context is projected to 6 dimensions via a learned linear layer before encoding into circuit phases.
problem_formulation.objective_function: End-to-end minimization of prediction error for next latent code and reconstructed swaption surface.

problem_instance.description: Same swaption surface next-day prediction task as the main experiment.

dataset_specification.description: 494 daily 224-dimensional surfaces; same train/validation/test split and preprocessing as main experiment.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Same preprocessing pipeline and autoencoder compression; quantum model uses learned linear projection from 120 to 6 dimensions before phase encoding.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Held-out 6-day test set; trained with Adam for 200 epochs.

noise_model.noise_description: classically simulated photonic circuits; no explicit noise model reported

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Same preprocessing pipeline as main experiment; learned linear projection from 120 to 6 dimensions before quantum encoding
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Linear readout maps Fock probabilities to 20 latent predictions; decoder reconstructs surface

speedup_claims.caveats: No speedup claim is reported; the model is presented as a baseline and performs worse than classical methods.

experiments.description: Hybrid variational-recurrent quantum LSTM baseline where each LSTM gate is augmented with a variational photonic circuit.

algorithm.ansatz: Variational photonic circuit with RY encoding gates and CNOT entanglement inside each gate

problem_formulation.encoding_details: The 20-dimensional latent input is projected to 4 dimensions via a learned linear layer before amplitude encoding into the variational circuit.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Hybrid recurrent prediction of next latent code using quantum-augmented LSTM gates.

problem_instance.description: Same swaption surface next-day prediction task as the main experiment, using latent sequences of length 5.

dataset_specification.description: 494 daily 224-dimensional surfaces; temporal window length k=5; same train/validation/test split.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Same preprocessing and autoencoder compression; latent sequence input of length 5; 20-dimensional latent codes projected to 4 dimensions before quantum encoding.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Held-out 6-day test set; trained with Adam for 200 epochs.

noise_model.noise_description: classically simulated photonic circuits; no explicit noise model reported

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Same preprocessing pipeline as main experiment; temporal windowing with k=5; learned projection from 20 to 4 dimensions before quantum encoding
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Quantum outputs feed into LSTM gates and FC→GELU→FC readout head

speedup_claims.caveats: No speedup claim is reported; the model is slower and less accurate than classical baselines.
